meta.description: Post-1956 disasters and major events (Sudan/South Sudan). Figures only as quoted; no fatality figures. Arabic titles are working translations.

figures.text: nearly 1 million families saw their houses being damaged or completely destroyed

citation.quote: Sudan had not faced such levels of destruction due to rains since 1988, when nearly 1 million families saw their houses being damaged or completely destroyed by the storms.

In 1998, Sudan faced its most serious humanitarian crisis in more than a decade when the combination of a five-year drought and intensified conflict produced a major famine in the Bahr Al Ghazal region that put nearly 800,000 persons at risk of starvation. ... By early June, ... the number of people in need of food assistance was found to have risen to 795,000 persons.

figures.text: 1.65 million internally displaced persons in Darfur, and more than 200,000 refugees from Darfur in neighbouring Chad

citation.quote: according to United Nations estimates there are 1.65 million internally displaced persons in Darfur, and more than 200,000 refugees from Darfur in neighbouring Chad.

figures.text: over 128,000 people whose houses were destroyed or damaged (Khartoum State)

citation.quote: Khartoum State is severely affected with over 128,000 people whose houses were destroyed or damaged by heavy rains and floods, according to the FMoH.

title.en: 2020 floods and national state of emergency

citation.quote: The situation led the Transitional Government of Sudan to declare, on 4 September, a national State of Emergency for the next three months ... Over 506,000 people have been affected since the start of the rains in mid-July

citation_2.quote: the number of people critically affected has exceeded 730,000 on 16 September, according to the Government’s Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC).

figures.text: An estimated 8,585,611 internally displaced persons (IDPs) were recorded across all 18 states.

citation.quote: An estimated 8,585,611 internally displaced persons (IDPs) were recorded across all 18 states. An estimated 5,273,334 returned individuals were recorded across nine states.

records.place_note: Zamzam camp, ~12 km south of El Fasher (zamzam not in cities db)

figures.text: population expanding rapidly over the past weeks to at least 500,000 people

citation.quote: “has severely impeded humanitarian access and pushed parts of North Darfur into famine, notably in the Zamzam camp for internally displaced persons (IDPs)”, stated the Famine Review Committee of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)
The Federal Ministry of Health of Sudan declared a cholera outbreak on 12 August 2024 after confirmation of samples from Kassala State, which has been reporting suspected cases since 22 July 2024.
